facts_of_case: The respondent-wife performed second marriage during pendency of FAO No.290-M-2008. The petitioner-husband challenged the judgment and decree dated 19.8.2008 granting decree of divorce in favour of respondent-wife.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse cannot remarry during the pendency of an appeal.
legal_principles.held: Even if no stay is granted against a decree of divorce, the respondent cannot remarry during the pendency of the appeal.
cited_cases: Savitri Pandey Vs. Prem Chandra Pandey, 2002(1) RCR (Civil) 719

legal_principles.principle: A party to a dissolved marriage can marry again if the period for filing an appeal has expired or the appeal has been dismissed.
legal_principles.held: It necessarily implies that the decree holder has to make inquiries that no appeal has been filed within the period of limitation or that the appeal has been dismissed.

legal_principles.principle: The Appellate Court is enjoined to perform functions required by the trial court.
legal_principles.held: Although no such express provision has been made imposing similar obligation on the first Appellate Court by Section 28 of the 1955 Act, yet the Appellate Court is enjoined upon performing such functions which are required to be performed by the trial Court that has passed the decree and statutory guidance is available under Section 96 of the Civil Procedure Code.

outcome.final_order: The court granted a decree of divorce on the ground of cruelty in favour of respondent-wife.

use_for_drafting: responding to allegations of cruelty and desertion
